## Warm-up · Your missing readings {#warmup .activity}

[Pairs · 8 minutes · your homework example]{.act-label}

::: {.prompt}
Tell your neighbor the reading you brought: what went missing, and why.
:::

::: {.checks3}
::: {.c4}
[1 · What stopped it]{.label}
A fault, a schedule, a person, or the process itself?
:::
::: {.c4}
[2 · When]{.label}
At random times, at the same time each day, or only in certain conditions?
:::
::: {.c4}
[3 · The value]{.label}
Would the missing value have been higher, lower, or the same as the rest?
:::
:::

[Keep question 3 in mind. It decides whether any fill method can be trusted.]{.note-line}

::: {.selfstudy}
Studying alone: write down one example and answer the three questions.
:::

## Three reasons a value goes missing {#why}

::: {.why3}
::: {.w}
[Unrelated to anything]{.label}
**A random loss.** A data packet is dropped, a cable is knocked.
[Effect: fewer data, no bias.]{.eff}
[Statisticians call this MCAR.]{.term}
:::
::: {.w}
[Related to something recorded]{.label}
**A schedule or a condition you can see.** The analyzer calibrates every night at 04:00.
[Effect: bias, unless you compare like with like.]{.eff}
[MAR: the reason is in the data.]{.term}
:::
::: {.w .hard}
[Related to the missing value]{.label}
**The value itself.** The analyzer goes over range when the concentration is high.
[Effect: bias that no fill method removes.]{.eff}
[MNAR: the reason is the value that is gone.]{.term}
:::
:::

[The third kind is common in plants: instruments fail, and operators skip samples, exactly when the process is unusual.]{.note-line}

## What the data can tell you {#diagnose}

::: {.checks4}
::: {.c4}
[By time]{.label}
Share missing by hour of day and day of week. A peak at one hour points to a schedule.
:::
::: {.c4}
[By length]{.label}
Single hours or long blocks? Long blocks are outages, and they hold most of the missing hours.
:::
::: {.c4}
[Against another tag]{.label}
Is the gap more likely when a related tag is high? A temperature, a load, a second sensor.
:::
::: {.c4}
[At the edges]{.label}
Are the values just before and after the gap unusually high or low?
:::
:::

::: {.bridge}
These checks can point to the third kind of gap. They cannot prove it: the value that caused the gap is the value you do not have.
:::

## Activity 1 · Six gaps, three reasons {#act1 .activity data-hold="true"}

[Pairs · 12 minutes · no computer needed]{.act-label}

```{=html}
<div class="stories" id="stories">
  <div class="story"><p>A flow signal drops out for a minute at random times when a forklift passes the cable tray.</p><button type="button">Reveal</button><p class="ans" hidden><b>Unrelated.</b> Short and random: fill short gaps; little bias.</p></div>
  <div class="story"><p>A gas analyzer runs an automatic zero check every night at 04:00 and records nothing.</p><button type="button">Reveal</button><p class="ans" hidden><b>Recorded: time.</b> Dropping it raises the daily mean. Fill from neighboring hours.</p></div>
  <div class="story"><p>A level gauge stores nothing while the tank is above 95 %.</p><button type="button">Reveal</button><p class="ans" hidden><b>The value.</b> Any fill stays below 95 %. Report the time above range; use the high-level alarm.</p></div>
  <div class="story"><p>No lab samples are taken on public holidays.</p><button type="button">Reveal</button><p class="ans" hidden><b>Recorded: calendar.</b> Fine if you compare like days; holiday operation may differ.</p></div>
  <div class="story"><p>Operators skip the shift sample when the unit is upset and they are busy.</p><button type="button">Reveal</button><p class="ans" hidden><b>The value.</b> The record looks calmer than the plant was.</p></div>
  <div class="story"><p>A pH probe is out for cleaning for three days.</p><button type="button">Reveal</button><p class="ans" hidden><b>Unrelated, but long.</b> Do not draw a line across three days. Leave it missing or use similar days, and report it.</p></div>
</div>
```

For each gap: which of the three reasons is it, and what would a plain mean of the remaining data get wrong? Decide before you reveal.
:::

## Six gaps, the answers {#act1-key}

| Gap | Reason | What goes wrong if you ignore it |
|---|----|-----------------|
| Forklift dropouts | Unrelated | Little: fewer data |
| Zero check at 04:00 | Recorded: time of day | A daily mean without the night hours is too high |
| Gauge over range | The missing value | Every fill stays below the range; the overflow time is lost |
| No samples on holidays | Recorded: calendar | Holiday operation is never seen |
| Samples skipped when upset | The missing value | The process looks more stable than it was |
| Probe out for three days | Unrelated, but long | A straight line across three days invents a calm process |

[Two of the six cannot be fixed by any method applied to the data alone. They can only be reported, or measured another way.]{.note-line}
